feed.title: NPR Topics: Science
feed.subtitle: The latest health and science news. Updates on medicine, healthy living, nutrition, drugs, diet, and advances in science and technology. Subscribe to the Health & Science podcast.

entry.title: The Trump administration weakens fuel efficiency standards for new cars
entry.summary: The Trump administration says easing these standards will make cars more affordable. Critics say it's not so simple and could be costly for the environment.

entry.title: SpaceX's Starship launches on first orbital mission from Texas
entry.summary: Starship is key to SpaceX's commercial success and NASA's plans to land humans on the moon. This is the 14th flight of the uncrewed Starship, but the first time it reached orbit.

entry.title: How to limit the rat numbers? Train the humans
entry.summary: D.C.'s Rat Rangers take anyone who is interested on night time safaris through some of the Capitol's filthiest back alleys to learn the way of the rats, and to be better humans.

entry.title: Mexico's Baja California braces for Hurricane Polo as Hurricane Nolo threatens Hawaii
entry.summary: Hurricane Nolo edged further away from the Hawaiian Islands on Sunday as major Hurricane Polo bore down on Mexico's Baja California peninsula with a threat of storm surge, high winds and heavy rains.

entry.title: Scientists discover two new species of sea spiders along Canadian coastline
entry.summary: So far, scientists have identified more than 1,300 species of sea spiders.

entry.title: We're looking for life on other planets. Are we ready to find it?
entry.summary: In 1960, astronomer Frank Drake listened for signals from alien worlds. Reporter Brendan Byrne's podcast When We Find Them picks up the search and asks what would happen if we finally find something.

entry.title: The hot spot: World Sauna Congress convenes in Oslo as global interest skyrockets
entry.summary: At the World Sauna Congress in Oslo, NPR's Will Stone covers how scientists and enthusiasts are exploring heat exposure as a growing global trend to boost wellbeing and fight social isolation.

entry.title: The Pacific is churning with hurricanes. The Atlantic is quiet. Blame El Niño
entry.summary: The Pacific Ocean has had an unusual number of storms this year, while the Atlantic hasn't recorded a single full-blown hurricane. Scientists point to an exceptionally strong El Niño.

entry.title: Years after storms, clean-up crews meticulously separate the sentimental from the wreckage
entry.summary: Across the country, lost-and-found networks seek to reunite objects with disaster survivors. The work can take years. In some cases, it's impossible to pick up all the pieces.

entry.title: These 6 charts show how NIH research funding has been reshaped under Trump
entry.summary: Stories of science funding being cut, labs shutting down and scientists losing jobs have flooded the media under Trump's administration. These six graphics show how those changes have affected U.S. biomedical research.
